findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Justify the bespoke DELETE retry/throttle wrapper against bd80's mandated dispatch_apply_phases._call_with_retry route — state why the existing 429/Retry-After-aware wrapper (max_retries=3, [1,2,4] delays, no throttle) is insufficient for a 30k-call run, or reuse it as the precedent directs.
evidence: Plan: 'DELETE does NOT go through delete_comment/_direct_rest_delete... Every request goes through the script's own wrapper, which honours Retry-After on 429 and backs off exponentially on 5xx'

bd80 precedent (cited as 'the established precedent, whose mechanism is reused here'): 'wrap each DELETE call through dispatch_one._call_with_retry, which is the repo's one existing 429+Retry-After-aware retry... Do NOT hand-roll a second retry layer.'

Codebase: dispatch_apply_phases.py:76-134 _call_with_retry already retries 429 honoring an integer Retry-After and 5xx with jittered backoff — but caps at max_retries=3 with a fixed [1,2,4] delay table and has no per-call throttle, a plausible (but unstated) reason to diverge for a 30k-call run
findings.finding: The plan hand-rolls its own 429/Retry-After retry+throttle wrapper for the ~30k DELETEs but does not reconcile this against the cited prior art (bd80), which chose the repo's existing shared wrapper dispatch_apply_phases._call_with_retry and explicitly said 'Do NOT hand-roll a second retry layer.' The plan's stated rationale only rules out the delete_comment/_direct_rest_delete helpers, not _call_with_retry (which already honors Retry-After on 429 and backs off on 5xx), so the divergence from the precedent's retry route is a re-implementation left unjustified.
scenarios: A reviewer or operator asks why bd80's mandated retry route was replaced with a bespoke wrapper for the identical operation class
Sustained 429s across ~30k DELETEs where the existing wrapper's 3-retry cap would exhaust — the actual justification for a custom wrapper — is never surfaced
findings.suggested_fix: Add one sentence to the rate-limiting bullet: either (a) route DELETEs through the existing dispatch_apply_phases._call_with_retry as bd80 did, or (b) explicitly note that _call_with_retry's max_retries=3 cap and absence of a per-call throttle are inadequate across ~30k calls under sustained 429s, which is why a purpose-built wrapper (unbounded Retry-After honoring + throttle) is used here.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the auth precondition for the DELETE surface (bot account holds 'Delete comments' permission on every affected project) and define 403 handling (abort-and-report, distinct from the idempotent 404).
evidence: Plan states 'A 404 on DELETE is idempotent success, so re-runs are safe' but says nothing about 403/permission
T3 checklist item (c): 'Auth/HTTPS preconditions stated'
DELETE /rest/api/3/issue/{key}/comment/{id} confirmed in acli_graph.py:567 (probe-validated 204), but the permission precondition to delete bot-authored comments is not named
findings.finding: The plan depends on ~30k authenticated Jira DELETE calls but never states the auth/permission precondition: the bot account must hold the Jira 'Delete comments' (own or all) project permission on every affected project. Only the 404 case is addressed (idempotent success); a 403 (permission-denied) is unhandled and would systematically abort the run.
findings.location: Mechanism — 'Rate limiting — 429 IS retried' bullet; Safety plan
scenarios: The bot token can post comments but lacks delete-comment permission on one project — the run aborts partway or before the first delete
A subset of the 30 issues live in a project with a different permission scheme
findings.suggested_fix: Add an auth precondition line ('bot accountId 712020:6471376f… holds Delete-comments permission on all affected projects, verified before --execute') and specify that a 403 aborts the issue and is reported, never retried.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Document the concrete restore/back-out procedure (how backup/<KEY>.json is replayed to re-POST deleted comments) so the backup is an actual reversibility mechanism, not just an acknowledgement.
evidence: 'Pre-deletion backup of the FULL comment payload (id, ADF body, author accountId + display name, created) per issue, written and completeness-checked BEFORE any DELETE.'
T4 requires the reversibility MECHANISM (explicit rollback/back-out), not just that a backup exists; no step describes re-posting comments from backup if post-verification fails.
findings.finding: The operation is irreversible (mass Jira comment DELETE); the plan captures a full-payload pre-deletion backup but never describes the restore/back-out procedure that turns the backup into an actual rollback.
scenarios: Per-issue post-verification detects a missing distinct body after deletes and the operator must re-create the wrongly deleted comments from backup/<KEY>.json
findings.suggested_fix: Add a safety bullet: 'Restore path: if post-verification finds MISSING>0 on an issue, re-POST the affected comment bodies from backup/<KEY>.json via the same retry-wrapped client; DELETE is 404-idempotent so re-runs are safe.'

evidence: 'A comment whose pre-strip rendered text lacks the marker is treated as foreign and is NEVER a deletion candidate in phase 1.'

'Post-deletion re-fetch shows zero missing distinct bodies ... confirmed independently against the backups (MISSING=0)' — this is a post-hoc live oracle; no fixture-level test of the classifier itself is described.
Detection logic is reused verbatim from outbound_comments.py (existing module) and bd80 precedent, which mitigates but does not fully replace a controlled classifier test.
findings.finding: The safety-critical marker-detection and dedup-grouping logic is validated only by live post-execution re-fetch, with no pre-execution test against a controlled fixture that proves adf.adf_to_text(body) marker detection and _normalize_comment_body grouping classify a mixed set (marked / unmarked-foreign / truncation-suffix) exactly as claimed before ~30k irreversible DELETEs run.
findings.location: Mechanism section ('Bot identification — the safety-critical filter') and Safety plan
scenarios: A future re-run or a change to the marker/normalization constants silently misclassifies a foreign/human comment as a deletion candidate; the live re-fetch only checks surviving-body invariants, not that a foreign comment was correctly excluded, so a wrong-classification of a one-copy foreign body could delete it undetected.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Qualify the 'exactly what the reconciler means by it' parity claim: note that the reconciler's outbound membership test also applies `sanitizer.fit_comment` + `codec.normalize_outbound` (outbound_comments.py:440-441) which the cleanup grouping omits, so parity holds only for bodies under the truncation limit — and state that steady-state '0 re-adds' is NOT guaranteed for the deferred Phase-2 truncation class.
evidence: Plan: 'Group candidates by outbound_comments._normalize_comment_body(body), imported and reused verbatim, so "distinct body" means exactly what the reconciler means by it.'

outbound_comments.py:440-441: `compare_body = _normalize_comment_body(codec.normalize_outbound(sanitizer.fit_comment(body)), ...)` — the reconciler's body-equality test additionally applies fit_comment + normalize_outbound, which the cleanup's grouping does not.
The inert comment_ids map (bug aa7b) means the lossy body-membership fallback is the ONLY dedup the live reconciler has, so this divergence is exactly the path that decides re-adds on re-enable.
findings.finding: The plan's stated parity guarantee — that grouping by `_normalize_comment_body(body)` makes 'distinct body' mean 'exactly what the reconciler means by it' — is stronger than the code supports: the reconciler's outbound body-membership fallback compares `_normalize_comment_body(codec.normalize_outbound(sanitizer.fit_comment(body)))` (outbound_comments.py:440-441), applying fit-to-limit truncation and outbound normalization that the cleanup's grouping omits. For over-length / truncation-affected bodies (the same class Phase 2 addresses) the two notions of 'distinct' can diverge, so the kept representative may not match what the reconciler would consider already-mirrored.
findings.location: Mechanism section — 'Dedup key = the reconciler's OWN normalization' bullet
scenarios: A truncation-suffixed or over-length body whose fit_comment-normalized form collides with another under the reconciler but is kept as a separate distinct body by the cleanup (or vice-versa)
bd80's own close comment records ~12 comments re-synced because the cleanup normalization 'collapsed more aggressively than the reconciler's own outbound dedup' — the same asymmetry

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State and validate the restore path for the pre-deletion backup (how a deleted comment is re-created and what metadata — created ts, author attribution — is unrecoverable), or explicitly label the operation DATA LOSS RISK: deletions are not restorable in place.
evidence: Plan captures 'id, ADF body, author accountId + display name, created' but describes no mechanism to re-create deleted comments from that payload

POST-ROLLBACK applicability (d): one-way transformation with no back-out — DELETE is irreversible; the plan asserts post-deletion state only via re-fetch, not that the backup constitutes a usable restore path
Keep-one invariant and post-verification reduce but do not eliminate the risk of an over-broad delete list (e.g. a mis-resolved bot accountId or normalization edge case)
findings.finding: The pre-deletion backup is the only stated back-out for an irreversible bulk DELETE, but the plan never asserts a restore/re-post path exists or was validated; Jira comment deletion cannot be reversed in place (re-POSTing loses original created timestamp and author attribution), so a completeness-checked backup does not by itself guarantee recoverability on partial-failure or mistaken deletion.
findings.location: Safety plan (T4 — irreversible): 'Pre-deletion backup of the FULL comment payload ... written and completeness-checked BEFORE any DELETE'
scenarios: A phase-1 candidate is wrongly classified (e.g. a foreign comment whose rendered text coincidentally contains the marker) and deleted; the backup cannot faithfully restore its original created/author metadata
A partial run deletes the kept-oldest copy due to a normalization collision and no in-place restore is available
